entities.name: Pomegranate extract
observations: In hypercholesterolemic pigs, 10-day dietary pomegranate extract prevented impaired coronary endothelium-dependent relaxation and was associated with Akt/eNOS-axis activation, reduced MCP-1, and reduced oxidative DNA damage.

entities.name: Coronary endothelial dysfunction
observations: Hypercholesterolemic pigs developed impaired coronary relaxation that was prevented by pomegranate extract; human evidence for coronary-specific prevention remains unavailable in the identified trials.

entities.name: PI3K/Akt-eNOS pathway
observations: Red-wine polyphenols, grape-skin extract, grape juice, and EGCG induced coronary endothelial NO-mediated relaxation with Akt/eNOS phosphorylation; PI3K inhibitors, NOS inhibition, and redox interventions reduced responses.

entities.name: Red-wine polyphenols
observations: In isolated porcine coronary arteries, red-wine polyphenols increased NO/cGMP and Akt/eNOS-Ser1177 phosphorylation; L-NA, ROS scavengers, and PI3K inhibitors inhibited relaxation and signaling.

entities.name: Grape polyphenols
observations: Grape-skin extract and Concord grape juice produced coronary eNOS-dependent relaxation and ROS/Src/PI3K/Akt/eNOS signaling, with responses reduced by pathway inhibitors.

entities.name: Epigallocatechin gallate
observations: EGCG induced NO-mediated relaxation and Akt/eNOS phosphorylation in porcine coronary preparations; membrane-permeant SOD/catalase analogues inhibited the response.

entities.name: Systemic endothelial dysfunction
observations: In human chocolate trials, flavanol-rich or high-cocoa chocolate improved brachial flow-mediated dilation; one study also increased plasma NOx and reduced Nox2 activity and isoprostanes, without measuring coronary Akt/eNOS activation.
